html:
The Treaty of London of 1867 declared Luxembourg a permanently neutral state and ended the Luxembourg Crisis between France and Prussia.

In 1867 Napoleon III of France offered to buy Luxembourg from the Dutch king William III, who was also its grand duke. Prussia kept a garrison in the fortress and objected, and war seemed close. A conference of the great powers in London found a way out: the Prussian troops left, most of the fortress was to be pulled down, and Luxembourg was declared neutral under their guarantee.

Neutrality did not save the country from German occupation in both world wars, and it gave it up for NATO in 1949.
sum: The Treaty of London of 1867 declared Luxembourg a permanently neutral state and ended the Luxembourg Crisis between France and Prussia.
